must_fix_before_live.summary: THE COMPLETENESS PROOF IS BLIND TO THE OWNER-IMPORT PHASE, AND A MODULE LOAD IS WHERE THE FIFTH MEMBER LIVED. MECHANISM, read off the shipped tracer: scripts/selftest.py:19643 sets `ARMED = [False]', :19645 gates the hook on `if ARMED[0] and event == "open"', :19652 installs the hook, :19653-19655 then LOAD .warp/validate.py, .warp/intent_corpus.py and .warp/entropy.py, and only at :19656 does `ARMED[0] = True'. Every file those three module loads open is therefore DISCARDED BY CONSTRUCTION, on every tree, for every hand-off. MEASURED, not argued: I ran the tracer verbatim (extracted from _M10_R12_TRACER) over a full copy of this repository in which the only change was ONE import-time statement added to .warp/entropy.py, `_PROBE_UNDECLARED_ROOT = open(str(ROOT / ".warp" / "probe_root.json")).read()', a path that matches NO declared root of any hand-off. RESULT: architecture_contract 4 paths, spec_corpus 444, spec_area_index 139, entropy_series_owner 216, and `.warp/probe_root.json' appears in NONE of the four traces - so _M10_R12_UNDECLARED would be EMPTY and the gate would stay GREEN. THEN THE HARM, on the same tree: a FIFO at .warp/probe_root.json took `.warp/metrics.py', `--json', `.warp/dashboard.py' and `--html' each past a 12-second clock with ZERO bytes and NO exit code. 4 of 4 HUNG. That is R11-B1's harm exactly, reachable with a green gate, and the assertion built to make it a gate failure cannot see it. THE SENTENCES IT REFUTES, word for word: (a) .warp/metrics_read_closure.py:25-30, present in ALL EIGHT engine copies - `the closure is PROVEN COMPLETE BY MEASUREMENT rather than by reading an owner's code: the selftest runs each owner call under an interpreter AUDIT HOOK that records every path OPENED and asserts that not one lies outside the declared roots, so an owner that begins opening a new root fails the gate instead of wedging a surface'; (b) .warp/metrics_read_closure.py:50-51 - `a root nobody declared is a GATE FAILURE rather than a hang'; (c) the gate label at scripts/selftest.py:19734 - `This is the assertion that makes an owner opening a NEW root a gate failure instead of a wedged surface'; (d) proof/WARP-1210/manifest.json AC3 evidence 3 and AC6 evidence 9, which offer the audit-hook trace as the BACKING for the universal `every root any owner opens on this pass's behalf is DECLARED'. A SECOND, SMALLER OVERSTATEMENT IN THE SAME SENTENCE: scripts/selftest.py:19673-19675 does `try: _rel.add(...relative_to(ROOT)) except ValueError: continue', so every open OUTSIDE the tree is silently dropped and is asserted against by nothing - I measured 4 such opens per trace on this repository and 7 on the entropy hand-off, all stdlib bytecode. The gate label and the manifest DO scope this correctly (`every opened path inside the tree'); the shipped module docstring does not, and the module is the artifact an adopter reads. WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT ONLY A SENTENCE: the item's stated purpose for the trace is `so an owner that begins opening a new root fails the gate instead of wedging a surface', and residual 3 (assumptions[5]) declares exactly ONE limit on it - `if an owner opened a root only under an input neither tree exercises, the trace would not see it'. The limit I measured is different and larger: the trace cannot see an import-time root on ANY tree, so no third tree, no seeded root and no future fixture closes it. That is a hole in the mechanism, not in the fixture set, and it is undeclared. THE FIX IS ONE LINE AND I RAN IT: arm the hook from process start (`ARMED = [True]', or drop the flag). I traced all four hand-offs over this repository that way and the load phase adds exactly SEVEN in-tree opens, every one of them `.warp/__pycache__/*.pyc' - an ALREADY DECLARED ORGAN root - so arming from the start costs nothing, changes no declared row, and WOULD have caught the probe above. The honest alternatives are to make the claim true that way, or to DELETE the forward-looking clause from all eight copies, the label and the manifest and state the measured scope instead: the closure is proven complete over what the four owner CALLS open INSIDE the tree, on two trees.

residual_rulings.RESIDUAL 1 (assumptions[2]) - the corpus: TRADEOFF, and I ruled it by the owner's own test rather than by accepting the word `over-broad on purpose': does an ORDINARY condition stand the section down? NO, and I measured eight of them on a full copy of this repository, four surfaces each, 32 runs: a STALE pyc (source touched newer), a TRUNCATED pyc (4 bytes), a ZERO-BYTE pyc, a leftover `validate.cpython-312.pyc.12345' from an interrupted atomic write, a mode-000 pyc, NO `__pycache__' directory at all, `__pycache__' replaced by a regular FILE, and a read-only `__pycache__' that cannot be rewritten. EVERY ONE rendered BYTE-IDENTICALLY to baseline (701 / 4935 / 1940 / 4538). The reason is structural and sits in the predicate at .warp/metrics_read_kind.py:152-160: an entry is refused only if it EXISTS, resolves through os.stat, and is NEITHER a regular file NOR a directory - so every ordinary bytecode pathology is a regular file or an absent path and is never refused, an absent path is never refused, and a symlink to a regular file is followed and not refused. The section is reachable only by a FIFO, a socket or a device, which is a deliberate act. This is over-breadth, not a section that will be down in normal operation, and the fail-closed direction is the only one available given the owner reads those roots with a bare read_text().
